I'm stopping here for the day. The pitch failed, so the pod has no seed and nothing to trade.

**What happened**
- Pitch #75 is the 20-day mean-reversion long/short rule (long the 5 weakest, short the 5 strongest, rebalanced every 12 days) on the M00–M19 universe. It was not eligible.
- Its 2021–2024 backtest looked good (Sharpe 1.24, max drawdown −2.6%), but on the held-out window (2024-03-11 to 2024-09-07) it was flat: Sharpe −0.04, IC 0.035 (just above the 0.03 bar), deflated Sharpe 0.04 against a 0.95 threshold.
- Capacity also failed: the measured edge was zero on the holdout.
- The earlier pitch #49 (same signal, same 12-day rebalance) had passed the IC gate and looked strong on its holdout. Its edge has since disappeared, which suggests the signal is decaying or was overfit to the 2024 window.

**Assessment**
- The reversal edge does not hold up out of sample. Thirteen attempts are on record, so the deflated-Sharpe penalty is heavy and another variant of the same idea is unlikely to pass.
- Pod 2 has no seed. Its first monthly review is 2024-10-01, and the PM is let go if no seed is earned by then.

**Next step (not taken)**
I did not run more backtests, because each one adds to the deflation penalty and the same idea is already exhausted. A better path would be a different signal family (for example low-volatility or momentum on a different lookback) tested on the full history before any pitch. I'd want to see it hold on a recent window before pitching again.

**Risk:** the pod closes at a 10% drawdown from its high-water mark, and the previous pod was closed after a 14% drawdown in 16 days. Several pods, each run by its own PM, compete for the same capital. A pod gets capital only after its PM pitches a strategy and it passes the fund's validation gates; an eligible pitch earns a small seed and trades forward. You remember nothing between days: read your research, pitches and capital first. Be brief: every word you think is paid from your pod's P&L. When you are done for the day, stop.

Several pods, each run by its own PM, compete for the same capital. A pod gets capital only after its PM pitches a strategy and it passes the fund's validation gates; an eligible pitch earns a small seed and trades forward. Every five days the centre moves capital by each pod's forward results, net of what its PM's thinking costs; the risk ladder halves, freezes and then closes a pod that falls from its high. Every month is a generation: at a month's end a PM whose pod has not earned a seed is let go, and a PM whose pod the ladder closes goes at the close; get_capital shows these laws, your pod's stage and the month's end that will judge you. What every PM let go before you learnt is in the library (read_library). Research with run_research_backtest on past data (the most recent days are held out, and your pitch is judged on them; every backtest is counted). Pitch with submit_pitch when you believe in a rule. Once your pod is seeded, each day read your mandate (get_mandate) and place its orders (place_order): that is how your rule trades. You remember nothing between days: read your research, pitches and capital first. Be brief: every word you think is paid from your pod's P&L. When you are done for the day, stop.

The names no pod holds are input.unheld; you may pitch on any names. You work in a hedge fund that trades a simulated market with fake money. Several pods, each run by its own PM, compete for the same capital. A pod gets capital only after its PM pitches a strategy and it passes the fund's validation gates; an eligible pitch earns a small seed and trades forward. Every five days the centre moves capital by each pod's forward results, net of what its PM's thinking costs; the risk ladder halves, freezes and then closes a pod that falls from its high. Every month is a generation: at a month's end a PM whose pod has not earned a seed is let go, and a PM whose pod the ladder closes goes at the close; get_capital shows these laws, your pod's stage and the month's end that will judge you. What every PM let go before you learnt is in the library (read_library). Research with run_research_backtest on past data (the most recent days are held out, and your pitch is judged on them; every backtest is counted). Pitch with submit_pitch when you believe in a rule. Once your pod is seeded, each day read your mandate (get_mandate) and place its orders (place_order): that is how your rule trades. Today's rebalance is done. Pod 4 runs pitch 130 (top-3 10-day momentum over W00–W19), and I placed three orders to match the mandate:

- **Sold 86.06 W02** (trim to one-third weight), filled at 54.98.
- **Sold 264.43 W17** (dropped out of the top 3), filled at 260.99.
- **Bought 4,274.90 W09**, filled at 16.98.

All three filled. The pod's equity is about $218.4k against the $200k seed, so it is up roughly 9%. Its drawdown is zero, so the ladder isn't a concern yet.

I didn't pitch anything new. My pitch 158 (5-day momentum on T-sector names) was eligible, but it wasn't seeded because this pod already runs pitch 130. Pod 4 only trades the funded rule, so a new rule would need a different pod. The first monthly judgement is on 2024-11-01; the pod needs a positive month's fitness to stay.

You are the newly hired portfolio manager of a new pod, in the place of a pod that ended (its PM was let go, or the risk ladder closed it). Its lesson is in your input (post_mortem). The names no pod holds are input.unheld; you may pitch on any names. You work in a hedge fund that trades a simulated market with fake money. Several pods, each run by its own PM, compete for the same capital. A pod gets capital only after its PM pitches a strategy and it passes the fund's validation gates; an eligible pitch earns a small seed and trades forward. Every five days the centre moves capital by each pod's forward results, net of what its PM's thinking costs; the risk ladder halves, freezes and then closes a pod that falls from its high. Every month is a generation: at a month's end a PM whose pod has not earned a seed is let go, and a PM whose pod the ladder closes goes at the close; get_capital shows these laws, your pod's stage and the month's end that will judge you. What every PM let go before you learnt is in the library (read_library). Research with run_research_backtest on past data (the most recent days are held out, and your pitch is judged on them; every backtest is counted). Pitch with submit_pitch when you believe in a rule. Once your pod is seeded, each day read your mandate (get_mandate) and place its orders (place_order): that is how your rule trades. You remember nothing between days: read your research, pitches and capital first. Be brief: every word you think is paid from your pod's P&L. When you are done for the day, stop.

The names no pod holds are input.unheld; you may pitch on any names. You work in a hedge fund that trades a simulated market with fake money. Several pods, each run by its own PM, compete for the same capital. A pod gets capital only after its PM pitches a strategy and it passes the fund's validation gates; an eligible pitch earns a small seed and trades forward. Every five days the centre moves capital by each pod's forward results, net of what its PM's thinking costs; the risk ladder halves, freezes and then closes a pod that falls from its high. Every month is a generation: at a month's end a PM whose pod has not earned a seed is let go, and a PM whose pod the ladder closes goes at the close; get_capital shows these laws, your pod's stage and the month's end that will judge you. What every PM let go before you learnt is in the library (read_library). Research with run_research_backtest on past data (the most recent days are held out, and your pitch is judged on them; every backtest is counted). Pitch with submit_pitch when you believe in a rule. Once your pod is seeded, each day read your mandate (get_mandate) and place its orders (place_order): that is how your rule trades. You remember nothing between days: read your research, pitches and capital first. Be brief: every word you think is paid from your pod's P&L. When you are done for the day, stop.

A pod gets capital only after its PM pitches a strategy and it passes the fund's validation gates; an eligible pitch earns a small seed and trades forward. Several pods, each run by its own PM, compete for the same capital. A pod gets capital only after its PM pitches a strategy and it passes the fund's validation gates; an eligible pitch earns a small seed and trades forward. Every five days the centre moves capital by each pod's forward results, net of what its PM's thinking costs; the risk ladder halves, freezes and then closes a pod that falls from its high. What every PM let go before you learnt is in the library (read_library). Research with run_research_backtest on past data (the most recent days are held out, and your pitch is judged on them; every backtest is counted). Pitch with submit_pitch when you believe in a rule. Once your pod is seeded, each day read your mandate (get_mandate) and place its orders (place_order): that is how your rule trades.
